name: NJ-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Frank Pallone's incumbency in a district with a five-point Democratic lean
Overwhelming fundraising gap: $3.1 million cash on hand versus under $1,000 for the challenger

model.rationale: Pallone combines incumbency with a commanding financial edge, out-raising Hillary Herzig by more than 200-to-1 and holding over $3 million in the bank against her $943. With a D+5 district lean, no outside spending against him, and markets pricing the race near 97 percent Democratic, no evidence points to a competitive race.
model.watch: A sharp national swing against Democrats or the emergence of serious outside spending for the challenger would be the main ways this margin narrows.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Frank Pallone, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election with every structural advantage in a district with a five-point Democratic lean. He has raised about $2.2 million and holds more than $3 million in cash on hand, while Republican Hillary Herzig has raised roughly $11,000 and reports under $1,000 available. No outside groups are spending in the race, and no public polls or expert ratings are on record.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent. The combination of incumbency, the district's partisan lean, and the enormous financial gap points to a comfortable Democratic margin. With so little money and no visible campaign infrastructure on the Republican side, an upset would require an unusually large national shift against Democrats. The race sits in the Safe Democratic column.
